bullets: A great RFC starts with context and constraints, then options, rather than leading with a proposed solution; this pattern recurs at teams using Notion, PagerDuty, and Datadog.
Writing things down turns disagreement into collaboration, and skipping it means rebuilding the decision from scratch a year later — the second-order effect most people miss.
Postmortems that focus on individuals miss the system that made the mistake easy, a pattern observed at teams using Sentry, Notion, and Datadog.
Architecture decisions are mostly tradeoffs, and the framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs are actually being made rather than hiding them.
Risk management is a communication problem rather than a purely technical one; its trade-offs cross-cut every other engineering communication topic, as seen at teams using Linear and Notion.
Good on-call rotations are designed so waking up is rare, which ties reliability directly to how engineering teams communicate and plan.
These communication patterns held consistently across three different teams, and tools like Sentry and PagerDuty are where they show up most cleanly.
Adopting one covered idea and running it for two weeks is the recommended starting point — the rest is iteration rather than wholesale process change.
